task.problem:
Let X be connected and compact, dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, and fix a smooth positive probability volume dV. All potentials are genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, with pole values included. A smooth real (1,1) background theta is big if theta+dd^c rho>=epsilon h for a genuine potential rho, a Hermitian h and epsilon>0; it need not be closed. Ordinary order u preceq v means u<=v+C, and equivalence is mutual order. I(tu) uses |g|^2 exp(-tu), with no extra factor 2; ideal equivalence means equality at every real t>0. P_(theta,F)[u] is the usc supremum of theta-psh v<=F with v preceq u; P_(theta,F)[u]_I uses ideal-equivalent competitors. The zero-obstacle operations are P_theta[u] and P_theta[u]_I. An ordinary model is a normalized fixed point p=P_theta[p], and an ideal model also satisfies p=P_theta[p]_I. Extended products are non-pluripolar products with smooth-background corrections. Lower and upper singularity volumes are the infimum and supremum of extended mass over the entire fixed ordinary type, not the raw mass of one representative. BMP means finite supremum v_+(h) over all bounded h-psh potentials, and positive lower mass means the corresponding infimum v_-(h)>0; these are separate properties. Original S06 asks for type-sensitive regularity and stability criteria for equations in arbitrary prescribed ordinary or relative envelope types on smooth big possibly nonclosed backgrounds, beyond resolved logarithmic and exceptional minimal cases. At density zeros, find conditions on density and residual geometry yielding a smooth or Holder residual, and distinguish regularity on the complement from extension across the singular set. The relative envelope class E_env(X,theta,phi) consists of u preceq phi such that for every t>=1 some theta-psh a satisfies t^(-1)a+(1-t^(-1))phi<=u. Envelope equality is not its unrestricted definition. Also address singular envelopes and weighted extremals outside the known uniform density-in-capacity regimes. For a compact non-pluripolar K, continuous obstacle w and selecting potential phi, one precise weighted ideal envelope is the usc supremum of theta-psh a ideal-more-singular than phi with a<=w quasi-everywhere on K. Ideal order means I(ta) subset I(t phi) for every t>0. Declare any different ordinary or weighted version explicitly. Known background: local continuity above a locally bounded strict barrier, local Holder control for minimal Lp solutions, and smoothness on the full regular locus of an analytic strict barrier with smooth positive density are established under their precise hypotheses. Resolved logarithmic positive residuals and specified exceptional minimal types have quantified Holder remainders. Smooth positive global volume forms give ample-locus smoothness in every closed big Kahler class. Smooth density only on a smaller open set can accompany a discontinuous bounded solution. Smooth density zeros and their necessary exceptional vanishing order alone do not imply a smooth Hessian; explicit compact power-blowup and Pogorelov cases are already known. Finite ramification pullback and nonclosed Hopf examples already describe specified smooth zeros and residuals. A smooth positive dual maximizer already forces a smooth exact threshold equation, even at zeros. None of these settles arbitrary prescribed types or all singular extremals. No new regularity criterion, type, geometry or proof is supplied.

notes.detailedSummary: Records the ordinary psh supremum, restriction and extension tools, Bedford–Taylor continuity, non-pluripolar truncations, and the BMP hypothesis of the general Hermitian product extension. Independently checks Ahn’s finite continuous and Hölder weight hypotheses. Primary passages were saved through the web tool; direct shell downloads failed. No supplied proof or earlier notes were used.
notes.text:
Conventions and independently retrieved primary tools. Throughout D=i∂bar∂/(2π), d^c=i(bar∂−∂)/(4π), so dd^c=D. Wedges are ordinary wedges. Genuine quasi-psh representatives retain their canonical values, including −∞. No supplied or earlier notes existed.

The following foundational results are used with their stated hypotheses.

1. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter I, Theorems 5.5, 5.7, 5.11 and 5.24, author-hosted text: https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf . These give psh smoothing, the psh usc supremum for locally uniformly upper-bounded families, holomorphic restriction possibly identically −∞, and canonical extension across closed pluripolar sets under local upper boundedness. The distributional psh criterion applies to the canonical representative. Positive rescaling of D does not change these assertions.

2. Bedford–Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math. 149 (1982), 1–40, Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2: https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf . Locally bounded psh potentials have symmetric multilinear products continuous under decreasing psh approximation. Applications below concern bounded truncations or locally bounded potentials away from the pole.

3. Boucksom–Eyssidieux–Guedj–Zeriahi, Monge–Ampère equations in big cohomology classes, arXiv:0812.3674v2, Section 1.2, Proposition 1.6 and formula (1.7): https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2 . Non-pluripolar products use truncation and locality and discard pole sets; compact Kähler backgrounds guarantee finiteness for closed positive currents. Their closed Kähler uniqueness theory is not applied to arbitrary Hermitian products.

4. Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Volumes of Bott–Chern classes, Sections 2.1–2.2 and Theorem A: https://arxiv.org/html/2406.01090v1 . Bounded products use local psh shifts and smooth-background corrections. Their general global extension for all unbounded quasi-positive, quasi-closed currents requires BMP. Below, BMP is not assumed for arbitrary Y: the particular top-degree truncation limit is explicitly proved finite. Its mass is not identified with an infimum or supremum over an ordinary type.

5. Ahn, Characterization of continuity of Siciak–Zaharjuta extremal functions on compact Hermitian manifolds, arXiv:2604.01885v2, definitions (1.1)–(1.2), Theorem 1.4(ii): https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01885v2 . Weighted continuity assumes a finite continuous weight and continuous unweighted extremal. Ahn, Hölder regularity of Siciak–Zaharjuta extremal functions on compact Hermitian manifolds, arXiv:2604.01887v3, definition (1.2), Theorem 1.1(ii): https://arxiv.org/html/2604.01887v3 . Weighted Hölder regularity assumes finite Hölder weight, Hölder unweighted extremal and uniform density in capacity. Neither theorem applies to the genuine −∞ weight ψ+F or proves regularity of its retained residual. Their operators also do not impose the original question’s ideal order.

Evidence and rerun record. Primary passages were independently retrieved on 2026-10-07 and saved in literature/web1.json through literature/web8.json. The attempted BGL finds in web8 returned mismatched source labels and are not used; direct BGL passages in web5–web7 are used. Run python retrieve.py > literature/retrieval.log to repeat the shell retrieval attempts. All returned 'Operation not permitted', recorded in literature/retrieval.json; full PDFs were not downloaded. The saved web responses contain the retrieved primary evidence. No author argument for A–H was supplied or imported. These tools support the independently reconstructed proofs below. The notes remain unverified drafts.

notes.summary: A proved: ψ has a genuine sublogarithmic pole and an explicitly strictly convex profile, including both canonical ends.
notes.detailedSummary: Derives exact first and second derivatives, proves 0<A′<1 and 0<A″≤1/4+α(1−α), and gives left and right asymptotics. Establishes genuine κ-psh extension with ψ(0)=−∞ and ψ=0 at infinity. In fact κ+Dψ≥(1−α)κ.
notes.text:
Proof of A. Fix k≥2 and 0<α<1. On the standard affine chart put r=|z|², x=log r, a(x)=log(1+e^x), p=e^x/(1+e^x), q=1−p and T=1−log p=1+log(1+e^(−x)). The specified standard normalized form is κ=Da(log r). Its normalization is independently checked in n5; no rescaling is introduced.

Since p′=pq and T′=−q, with b=αT^(α−1) we obtain
ψ′=qb,
A′=p+qb=1−q(1−b),
A″=pq(1−b)+α(1−α)q²T^(α−2).
Here 0<b≤α<1. Consequently 0<A′<1, A″>0, and A″≤Bα:=1/4+α(1−α).

As x→−∞,
A=1−(1−x)^α+O(e^x),
A′=α(1−x)^(α−1)+O(e^x),
A″=α(1−α)(1−x)^(α−2)+O(e^x).
These follow from T=1−x+O(e^x) and the derivative identities. Thus A→−∞, A/x→0, A′→0 and ψ/x→0. The pole is unbounded and sublogarithmic.

At +∞ set σ=e^(−x), t=log(1+σ). Then
A−x=t+1−(1+t)^α>0,
A−x=(1−α)σ−(1−α)²σ²/2+O(σ³),
A′=1−(1−α)σ+O(σ²),
A″=(1−α)σ+O(σ²).
Strict positivity follows from strict concavity of (1+t)^α. The defect A−x decreases to zero because A′<1; at the left end it tends to +∞.

For a smooth radial profile Q, the complex Hessian matrix of Q(log r) is (Q′/r)I+((Q″−Q′)/r²)bar z⊗z. Its eigenvalues are Q′/r with multiplicity k−1 and Q″/r in the radial direction. Therefore DA is positive off 0. The corresponding eigenvalue numerators for κ are p and pq. Since A′≥p and A″≥(1−α)pq, κ+Dψ≥(1−α)κ there.

A is locally bounded above and locally integrable near 0, since powers of |log r| are integrable against r^(k−1)dr. The psh extension theorem in n1 extends it canonically. Its limit is −∞, forcing the genuine value ψ(0)=−∞. Applying the same extension argument after subtracting a local potential of (1−α)κ preserves the strict current inequality across 0.

At infinity use [Z0:…:Zk], a chart Zj≠0 with j≥1, τ=Z0/Zj, ξi=Zi/Zj for i≠0,j, and S=1+Σ|ξi|². Then σ=1/r=|τ|²/S, and ψ=1−(1+log(1+σ))^α is smooth through τ=0 with value zero. A local total κ-potential is log S+(A−x)(log r). At τ=0 its normal quadratic coefficient is (1−α)/S>0 and its tangential Hessian is that of log S. Positivity extends smoothly there. Thus ψ is a genuine global κ-psh potential with precisely the specified ends; the stronger inequality κ+Dψ≥(1−α)κ holds globally.

notes.summary: C and the convex end assertions of D proved for every C² compactly supported F and every free component, including accumulating components.
notes.detailedSummary: The whole-line convex minorant is finite, lies between A±||F||∞ and has end slopes zero and one. It is affine on every strict-gap component, C¹, and has derivative Lipschitz constant sup max((A+F)″,0). Tangent-line cutoffs prove exact left contact and the unattained-zero right-contact case; an attained infimum forces the stated affine right tail.
notes.text:
Whole-line proof of C and the convex assertions in D. Let f=A+F, mF=||F||∞ and QF=sup_R max(f″,0)<∞. Define C as the supremum of all affine functions below f on the entire line. Tangents of A−mF are admissible, so
A−mF≤C≤f≤A+mF. (1)
Thus C is finite, convex and continuous. Every finite convex minorant is the supremum of its supporting lines, so it lies below C. This verifies the equivalent definition as largest convex minorant.

By n2 and (1), C(x)/x→0 at −∞ and →1 at +∞. A negative supporting slope violates the left upper bound; a slope greater than one violates the right upper bound. Hence every subgradient is in [0,1]. Convex difference quotients and the same asymptotics give derivative limits zero and one at the respective ends.

Let J={C<f}. Around x0∈J choose [u,v]⊂J sufficiently small that min(f−C)=δ>0 and osc C<δ on that interval. Replace C there by its chord. Convexity is preserved because the chord slope lies between the right derivative at u and the left derivative at v. The chord exceeds C by less than δ and therefore remains below f. Maximality forces C to equal this chord. Consequently C is locally affine on J and affine on every connected component, including any unbounded component. No finite-component assumption is used.

At a contact point s, comparison with f for positive and negative increments gives C′_+(s)≤f′(s)≤C′_−(s). Convexity gives the reverse ordering, so all are equal. At gap points C is affine. Hence C is differentiable everywhere; convexity then implies continuity of its derivative, since any derivative discontinuity would be a jump between distinct one-sided derivatives.

For a<b, if there is no contact in [a,b], the derivative increment is zero. Otherwise let s,t be the first and last contact in [a,b]. Affineness of the intervening end gaps gives C′(a)=C′(s) and C′(b)=C′(t). If s=t the increment is zero; otherwise
0≤C′(b)−C′(a)=f′(t)−f′(s)=∫_s^t f″≤QF(t−s)≤QF(b−a).
This proves exactly the stated estimate and C∈C^{1,1}, with 0≤C″≤QF a.e. Also C′(x)>0 at every finite x: a zero derivative would force C constant on the left ray, contradicting C→−∞. The derivative may equal one on a right ray.

Here are explicit sufficient end-cutoff inequalities. Choose u<v containing supp F. Write ℓ_t(x)=A(t)+A′(t)(x−t). As t→−∞,
A(t)−tA′(t)=−(1−α)(1−t)^α+O(1),
so ℓ_t(v)→−∞. Choose t_-<u satisfying ℓ_(t_-)(v)≤min_[u,v] f. For t≤t_- the inequality persists because dℓ_t(v)/dt=A″(t)(v−t)>0 for t<v. Since A′>0, ℓ_t≤f on [u,v]; elsewhere ℓ_t≤A=f. Thus ℓ_t is admissible and C(t)=A(t) for all t≤t_-. This is exact contact on a left end interval.

Let L=inf_R(f−x). It is finite and L≤0 by the end behavior. The line x+L is below f and therefore below C. If L is attained at y, C(y)=f(y)=y+L. Since C′≤1, for x≥y,
C(x)≤C(y)+x−y=x+L≤C(x).
Thus C=x+L on that entire ray.

If L<0, it is attained: f−x tends to +∞ at the left end and to zero at the right, so a minimizing sequence stays compact. The only remaining case is L=0 unattained. Then f−x>0 everywhere, and δ=min_[u,v](f−x)>0. As t→+∞, ℓ_t(x)−x→0 uniformly on [u,v], with maximum ℓ_t(u)−u. Choose t_+>v satisfying ℓ_(t_+)(u)−u≤δ. This persists for t≥t_+ because dℓ_t(u)/dt=A″(t)(u−t)<0. Again ℓ_t≤f globally, so C(t)=A(t) for all t≥t_+. These alternatives are exhaustive, including L=0 attained, and establish all claimed end assertions.

notes.summary: B, the residual part of D, and F proved for the full ordinary global obstacle over all competitors.
notes.detailedSummary: The full envelope is psh and U(k)-invariant, so its total radial profile is a convex minorant. The constructed C-profile is a genuine admissible global competitor, forcing equality. The residual is canonically zero near the pole, smooth near infinity and globally C^{1,1}, with explicit annular bounds. Residual sup-norm stability has constant one.
notes.text:
Proof of B over all competitors. Define U=C(log r)−a(log r) off 0. Convexity and C′≥0 make C(log r) psh, using the radial Hessian calculation and convex-profile smoothing for nonsmooth C. By n3, C=A on a left end, so U=ψ there and its canonical pole value is −∞. At infinity either C=A, giving U=ψ, or C=x+L, giving U=L−log(1+σ). The latter is smooth in the infinity coordinates of n2 and has local total κ-potential log S+L. Thus U is a genuine global κ-psh potential.

The bounds in n3 give |U−ψ|≤mF off the pole, U≤ψ+F everywhere and U≃ψ in ordinary order, with the same genuine pole. Therefore U is an admissible competitor.

Let E be the usc supremum over the entire declared family. It is nonempty because ψ−mF is a competitor. In every κ-potential chart, the local total potentials form a locally uniformly upper-bounded psh family; n1 makes their usc supremum psh. The obstacle ψ+F is usc, has limit −∞ at 0 and is continuous elsewhere. Hence regularization still gives E≤ψ+F everywhere, including the genuine pole. Also E≥ψ−mF.

U(k) acts by [Z0:Z′]↦[Z0:UZ′], preserves κ and the obstacle, and permutes all competitors. Thus E is invariant without restricting the original family. Transitivity on affine spheres gives a finite profile Q(x)=E+a. Its restriction to a complex line is nontrivial by the lower bound A−mF. A radial subharmonic function Q(log|ζ|²) has Q″≥0 distributionally, so Q is convex with its canonical continuous representative. Since Q≤A+F, Q≤C. The competitor U gives the reverse envelope inequality. Consequently
E_F=C(log r)−log(1+r)
with exactly the canonical global extensions stated above. The upper ordinary-order condition is automatic from this particular full obstacle, but retention of the resulting type also uses the lower bound. No ideal condition or quasi-everywhere relaxation is introduced.

Residual and quantitative D. Numerical subtraction of two −∞ values is undefined. Define R_F=E_F−ψ=C−A off 0 and extend it by zero at 0, as forced by equality on a neighborhood. It is exactly zero for x≤t_-. At infinity it is either identically zero or
R_F=L−[log(1+σ)+1−(1+log(1+σ))^α],
σ=|τ|²/(1+Σ|ξi|²).
This expression is smooth through σ=0. Its infinity value is L in the attained case and zero in the unattained case.

Globally in x,
||R_F||∞≤mF, |R_F′|≤1, |R_F″|≤QF+Bα a.e.
On a finite closed annulus a0≤log r≤b0, real Euclidean derivatives satisfy
|∇R_F|≤2e^(−a0/2),
||∇²R_F||op≤[4(QF+Bα)+2]e^(−a0) a.e. (2)
Indeed |∇log r|=2/√r and ||∇²log r||op=2/r. Thus every finite annulus, including accumulating free boundaries, has quantitative C^{1,1} control. The exactly zero left end, smooth right end and finite coordinate cover of the remaining annulus prove global C^{1,1} of the retained residual. This proves extension through the pole, not only complement regularity. E_F itself remains unbounded and is not asserted globally Hölder.

Proof of F. Set δ=||F−G||∞. The largest-convex-minorant operator is monotone and commutes with addition of constants. From A+F≤A+G+δ and the reverse inequality, |C_F−C_G|≤δ on R. Subtracting A and taking the continuous canonical end extensions gives
sup_(P^k)|R_F−R_G|≤||F−G||∞.
Both residuals vanish at the pole. This is only C⁰ stability; no derivative stability is inferred.

notes.summary: E proved: actual non-pluripolar mass is one, annular masses are the stated slope differences, and deep negative bumps force an open affine zero-density tail.
notes.detailedSummary: Derives the determinant density with the exact D normalization and identifies it with bounded Bedford–Taylor products. Lipschitz C′ eliminates sphere atoms. Truncation discards the genuine pole, while infinity contributes no singular mass. Affine gaps have rank k−1 for positive slope. The bump inequality forces an attained negative L and a strict free right tail.
notes.text:
Proof of E for the actual measure. On a finite annulus the local total κ-potential is C(log r), of class C^{1,1}. Let dλ_2k denote Euclidean volume. The eigenvalues calculated in n2 and ordinary wedge normalization give a.e.
(κ+DE_F)^k=(k!/π^k)(C′)^(k−1)C″r^(−k)dλ_2k. (3)
There is no extra factor two: (i/(2π))dz∧dbar z=(1/π)dx∧dy.

To identify this with the bounded-potential product, convolve the local psh potential on a slightly larger annulus with radial Euclidean smoothing kernels. These smooth psh potentials decrease to the canonical potential, have uniformly bounded Hessians on smaller annuli, and their Hessians converge at almost every Lebesgue point. Dominated convergence identifies their determinant limit with (3), while Bedford–Taylor continuity identifies it with the local product. This proves absolute continuity and excludes hidden free-boundary contributions.

With normalized sphere measure dν,
dλ_2k=[π^k/(k−1)!]r^(k−1)dr dν.
The pushforward under x=log r is therefore
k(C′)^(k−1)C″dx=d((C′)^k).
Since C′ is Lipschitz, (C′)^k is absolutely continuous. Thus for every finite a<b,
MA_κ(E_F)({a<log r<b})=C′(b)^k−C′(a)^k, (4)
and every sphere {log r=a} has zero mass.

Proof of G. Let Y be any connected compact complex m-fold with smooth positive Hermitian form h0. Write X=P^k×Y, π:X→P^k, H=π*κ+pr_Y*h0, N=k+m and V0=∫_Y h0^m. Closedness is not assumed. Exact canonical restriction. For any genuine H-psh v, work on a product coordinate box Uz×Uy. Choose a smooth local κ-potential b(z) and c>0 such that h0≤cD|w|² on Uy. Then
D[v+b(z)+c|w|²]≥cD|w|²−h0≥0.
Its genuine representative is psh. Restricting to w=w0 retains the actual values and is psh or identically −∞. The quadratic becomes constant on the slice, yielding exactly κ+D_z v(·,w0)≥0. There is no extra κ multiple or error term and no need for h0 to be closed.

The local restrictions glue. A slice nontrivial on one box cannot be identically −∞ on an overlapping open box, because a nontrivial psh function is locally integrable and cannot equal −∞ on an open set. Connectedness propagates this across P^k. Thus every slice is globally genuine κ-psh or identically −∞.

For every obstacle competitor, each genuine slice satisfies the full obstacle everywhere and the ordinary upper order. By n4 it lies below E_F everywhere; identically −∞ slices do also. Therefore every competitor v≤π*E_F. Conversely π*E_F is a genuine admissible H-psh potential since
H+Dπ*E_F=π*(κ+DE_F)+pr_Y*h0≥0.
Thus E_F^H=π*E_F with its canonical values. No symmetry of Y or reduction of the competitor family is used.

Actual extended measure. Away from {0}×Y, bounded local products and ordinary wedge expansion give only the term with k horizontal and m vertical factors:
MA_ext_H(π*E_F)=binom(N,k)MA_κ(E_F)⊗h0^m. (5)
To justify the global finite measure without BMP, take u_j=π*max(E_F,−j), bounded H-psh. Their bounded smooth-background-corrected products satisfy
(H+Du_j)^N=binom(N,k)(κ+Dmax(E_F,−j))^k⊗h0^m.
This follows by local smooth horizontal approximation, wedge expansion, dimensional vanishing of the other terms, and bounded Bedford–Taylor continuity. The vertical factor is smooth; closedness is unnecessary. Restrict to {E_F>−j}×Y and take the non-pluripolar limit. The finite base limit in n5 yields precisely (5), with no mass on {0}×Y. Therefore
∫_X MA_ext_H(E_F^H)=binom(N,k)V0.

notes.text:
Proof of H with exact constants. On C²\{0}, let rY=|ζ1|²+|ζ2|² and s=log rY. Direct differentiation gives
Ds=(i/(2π))Σ[δjl/rY−barζjζl/rY²]dζj∧dbarζl,
ds∧d^cs=(i/(2π))Σ[barζjζl/rY²]dζj∧dbarζl.
The second identity follows by expanding the specified d^c. Therefore
h0=Ds+ds∧d^cs=(i/(2πrY))Σ_(j=1)^2 dζj∧dbarζj.
It is smooth positive definite: Ds has rank one perpendicular to ζ and the second term fills the radial direction.

The deck map ζ↦eζ sends rY↦e²rY and s↦s+2. Hence ds,d^cs,Ds and h0 are invariant and descend. The action is free and properly discontinuous. Writing ζ=Rω identifies log R modulo one, so the quotient is diffeomorphic to S³×(R/Z), connected, compact and smooth, with its inherited complex surface structure.

For the closed form β=(i/(2π))Σdζj∧dbarζj, h0=rY^(−1)β. Thus
dh0=−ds∧h0=−ds∧Ds≠0.
At ζ=(R,0), R>0, ds=(2/R)dx1 and Ds=(1/(πR²))dx2∧dy2, so dh0=−2/(πR³)dx1∧dx2∧dy2. This proves actual nonclosedness after descent.

The one-form d^cs descends, making Ds=d(d^cs) globally exact on Y. It is semipositive of rank one everywhere. If Ω were Kähler, Ds∧Ω would be a strictly positive volume form, whereas Stokes gives
∫_Y Ds∧Ω=∫_Y d(d^cs∧Ω)=0.
This contradiction proves Y non-Kähler without a classification theorem. A Kähler form on P²×Y would restrict to a Kähler form on a slice Y, so the product is also non-Kähler. It is a connected compact complex fourfold. H=κ+h0 is positive and nonclosed because its derivative restricts to dh0 on that slice.

The exact normalization permits a further check. With dλ4 on the cover,
h0²=2/(π²R⁴)dλ4.
A radial fundamental domain is 1≤R<e and area(S³)=2π². Hence
V0=(2/π²)(2π²)∫_1^e dR/R=4.
By n6, with k=m=2 the actual envelope mass is binom(4,2)·4=24. This is a representative mass computation; no zero-lower-mass property, general BMP conclusion or acceptance flag is asserted.

The ordinary prescribed type is nonvacuous. Since ψ is unbounded, it is not ordinarily equivalent to the bounded minimal potential zero. Distinct exponents give distinct types: for 0<α<β<1, ψ_β−ψ_α=−T^β+T^α→−∞, so ψ_α≼ψ_β fails. These types have zero logarithmic coefficient but are unbounded; an analytic logarithmic singularity with zero coefficient is locally bounded. Thus they are not resolved logarithmic types.

Under the exact exp(−tψ) convention, all multiplier ideals are nevertheless trivial. For fixed t>0 and ε>0, sublogarithmic growth gives exp(−tψ)≤Cεr^(−ε) near zero. Choosing ε<k proves integrability against r^(k−1)dr. Holomorphic germs are bounded on smaller balls, so I(tψ)=O for every real t>0. The same proof applies on the product by integration in z. Both branches are ≤0, and εlog p−ψ tends to −∞ at the pole and is bounded above globally. Hence vε≃ψ and is an ordinary zero-obstacle competitor. At every point off zero, vε→0 as ε↓0.
